questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Honduras?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Honduras article.

questions.proof: Its capital and largest city is Tegucigalpa.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Honduras?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Honduras on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Honduras article.

questions.proof: It borders Guatemala, El Salvador and Nicaragua.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Honduras?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Trade” part of the Honduras article.

questions.proof: The currency is the Honduran lempira.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Honduras and _____ had tense relations throughout 2000 and early 2001 due to a boundary dispute off the Atlantic coast.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Honduras”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Foreign relations” part of the Honduras article.

questions.proof: Honduras and Nicaragua had tense relations throughout 2000 and early 2001 due to a boundary dispute off the Atlantic coast.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Several Latin American nations, including _____, temporarily severed diplomatic relations with Honduras.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “including”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Foreign relations” part of the Honduras article.

questions.proof: Several Latin American nations, including Mexico, temporarily severed diplomatic relations with Honduras.
